title: Priority 1 — Show one verifiable example of our engineering work
observation: The homepage names network assurance, guest WiFi, an AI helpdesk and business search, but provides no named project, attributable engineer or linked evidence. Its four automation examples are illustrations, not documented customer outcomes. The homepage is the only URL in the public sitemap.

changes.label: Content brief — not publication-ready copy
changes.before: The team section describes production platforms in general terms without a linked worked example.
changes.after: Add one concise, owner-verified project example beside the team section: the problem, what we built, our role, an attributable engineer and a public evidence link or permitted screenshot. Include measured results only when records support them. Preserve the existing offers and description. Draft exact copy after those facts are confirmed.

rationale: Highest-priority content improvement: give visitors and search systems specific, verifiable first-hand information that the current broad claims do not supply. This is supported practice, not a proven citation uplift.
applicability: Uses an existing expertise claim and strengthens its evidence. Start with one genuine project; no mass-generated service pages or invented case studies.
downside: Requires owner confirmation and permission for any customer material. Do not reveal confidential implementation details or imply the illustrative examples are client results.
rationale_confidence: High that the evidence gap exists; moderate that this is the best content investment until query evidence develops.
outcome_confidence: Unknown. Neither citation nor ranking improvement is established.
measurement: After exact copy is separately approved and published, record its date and URL, verify rendered text and links, then compare dated AI-answer observations, relevant Search Console queries and referrals. Keep other material edits stable; before/after changes are descriptive, not causal.

title: Priority 2 — Verify real AI-crawler access before changing access rules
observation: Public homepage returns HTTP 200 with readable HTML and no noindex/nosnippet restriction. robots.txt allows all agents. Google indexing and AI inclusion pass. This review has not verified genuine OpenAI, Anthropic or Perplexity crawler requests against origin/CDN logs.

changes.label: Verification task — no website copy or access change proposed
changes.before: Robots permission and ordinary HTTP access are confirmed; genuine AI search crawler access remains unverified.
changes.after: Check recent origin/CDN requests for OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot, verifying source identity against each provider’s published guidance. Record successful fetches or specific denials. If no request exists, record “not observed”. Propose only an evidenced, narrowly scoped fix for approval; leave authentication and security protections intact.

rationale: Close an important evidence gap in search eligibility without inventing a crawler blockage. An allowed robots file alone cannot establish that a CDN or firewall accepts genuine crawler requests.
applicability: Search crawlers differ from model-training crawlers. Do not broaden training permission as an SEO tactic. The existing permissive robots policy does not require redundant named Allow rules.
downside: Logs may lack sufficient retention or client-IP identity. A spoofed user-agent test is not proof; absence of a bot visit is not proof of blocking.
rationale_confidence: High for the need to distinguish robots permission from verified delivery; no current evidence of a block.
outcome_confidence: Unknown. Successful crawling is not a guarantee of citation or recommendation.
measurement: Record provider, verified request time, target URL, status and identity-validation method. Retain only necessary aggregate evidence; do not expose unrelated visitor logs.

title: Priority 3 — Establish a small AI-answer baseline
observation: The dashboard has search and referral imports, but this review has no saved, repeatable sample showing whether AI engines cite or recommend Unimpossible. Referrals cannot establish how often the site appears in answers.

changes.label: Measurement brief — no publishing or tracking installation proposed
changes.before: Search traffic and attributed referrals are available separately; AI-answer citations and recommendations are not yet sampled.
changes.after: Start with three fixed UK buyer questions: “Who can help a Norfolk business automate enquiry handling?”, “Who builds AI assistants for small UK businesses?”, and “What does UNimpossible do?”. Record the question, engine/product, date, locale, answer and cited URLs. Distinguish a mention, a citation and a recommendation. Repeat consistently before expanding the sample.

rationale: Measure the plugin’s actual goal directly, using a small repeatable sample alongside traffic. This is our proposed measurement experiment, not a provider requirement or a market-wide visibility score.

applicability: Questions derive from current public positioning, not proven customer demand. Start manually or reuse an existing approved tool. Do not buy a subscription or add a new monitoring platform for this review.
downside: Answers vary by model, location, session and time. Three questions cannot represent all demand; API answers may differ from consumer search products. Record failures rather than treating them as absence.
rationale_confidence: High that referrals and citations measure different things; provisional prompt selection.
outcome_confidence: Measurement provides evidence, not uplift. No prediction of future citations.
measurement: Compare repeated observations on the same questions and product surface. Report counts with their denominator and date, including no-answer/no-search runs separately. Keep referral requests, search impressions and enquiries distinct.
